bounds.domain: Two pre-existing identity buckets, wall time0..8 initially4, integer quarter-token units and two configurations exchanging the burst/sustained bottleneck. Each request needs four units from both buckets.
bounds.atomicity: One synchronous process-local consume call is atomic. The two keys represent already resolved service, organization, user and plan identities.
bounds.progress: No temporal or fairness claim. A stopped or backward clock may prevent refill indefinitely.

limitations: The finite integer scaling does not prove arbitrary JavaScript floating-point rounding, numeric overflow or invalid direct caller arguments.

Configuration changes, plan resolution and expiry, eviction/reset, cross-isolate traffic and distributed rate authority are outside the model. Eviction and reset intentionally create a new full local bucket.
Wall-clock time may move in either direction. Only new time above the retained per-bucket refill boundary adds tokens.

The conformance hook runs all named tests of the actual limiter, including rollback, partial refill, usable retry deadlines, paired refusal, service separation and response metadata. It is scenario evidence, not a general TypeScript refinement proof.
